asymmetric cell volume changes contribute to asymmetric cell morphologies in KV.
asymmetric changes in cell volume contribute to asymmetric cell morphology in the epithelium of KV.
asymmetric changes in cell volume and cell shape are regulated independently in KV, and these cell behaviors are regulated by ion flux and cell-cell adhesion, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate epithelial morphologies during tissue formation.
the mechanisms that control the shape and size of epithelial structures during development.
how the shape of epithelial cells changes during morphogenesis and how the changes in cell shape affect the shape of the tissue.

asymmetric cell volume changes regulate KV epithelial morphogenesis, independent of lumen - generated tissue forces.
asymmetric cell volume changes are a mechanism by which cells change shape in response to ion flux.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
asymmetric cell volume changes regulate asymmetric cell shape changes and that lumen expansion does not directly contribute to these changes in KV.
we show how asymmetric cell volume and cell shape changes contribute to the morphogenesis of a simple epithelium.

epithelial cells can change their volume independently of lumen expansion.
